title: Canonical coefficient reduction preserves pullback composition
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with completed coefficient sheaves and positive quotients [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale sites of schemes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $R_X$ be the actual whole-system derived coefficient reduction. Fix the system operations $o$ and section-normalized compositors $c$ of [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and a realization model $a$ of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. Write $\delta_f:R_X P_f^{\rm ring}\simeq P_f^{\rm sys}R_Y$ for its quotient/pullback comparison, fixed on K-flat complexes by the ordinary limit-projection normalization. For composable scheme maps $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$, let $\gamma^{\rm ring}_{f,g}:P^{\rm ring}_{fg}\simeq P_f^{\rm ring}P_g^{\rm ring}$ and $\gamma^{\rm sys}_{f,g}$ be the specified geometric compositors. For every completed-ring derived object $K$ on $Z$, the two arrows to $P_f^{\rm sys}P_g^{\rm sys}R_ZK$ agree: $P_f^{\rm sys}(\delta_g(K))\circ\delta_f(P_g^{\rm ring}K)\circ R_X(\gamma^{\rm ring}_{f,g}(K))=\gamma^{\rm sys}_{f,g}(R_ZK)\circ\delta_{fg}(K)$. This is an equality in the derived category of whole strict systems. No completeness, properness, constructibility or finite-amplitude hypothesis on $K,f,g$ is imposed.

proof.text: Geometric ringed pullback preserves flat-term K-flat complexes. Postcompose the desired derived equality on Q(P) with the invertible reduction and exact-pullback factors. Naturality moves the factors past the two reductionPull maps and the system compositor. Apply RealizationModel.model for f, g and fg, Compositors.pullComp_model, and the defining mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso factorization equations for ringedPullComp. Naturality of the reduction model moves the ordinary ringed compositor past that model. The two sides now have the same invertible initial factors followed by the derived localization of the whole-complex equality from the first step. Functoriality of Q and cancellation prove the desired equality on P.

proof.text: Form the two natural transformations with the components displayed in the statement. The flat-term K-flat localization is a localization of the good representative subcategory, so restriction along it is faithful on natural transformations. Apply Localization.natTrans_ext to the equality on each good representative and then take its component at the arbitrary derived object K. This uses whole systems throughout and makes no faithfulness assertion for finite derived evaluations.

theorem canonicalReductionPullComposition
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (o : IntegralSystemRealization.Operations l E)
    (a : IntegralSystemRealization.RealizationModel l E o)
    (c : IntegralSystemRealization.Compositors l E o)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E Z)) :
    (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E X).reduction.map
        ((IntegralSystemRealization.ringedPullComp l E f g).hom.app K) ≫
        (a.reductionPull f).hom.app
          ((IntegralSystemRealization.ringedPull l E g).obj K) ≫
        (IntegralSystemRealization.pull l E f).map
          ((a.reductionPull g).hom.app K) =
      (a.reductionPull (f ≫ g)).hom.app K ≫
        (c.pullComp f g).hom.app
          ((IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E Z).reduction.obj K)
